messages:
Maria L: Heads up — I got an email saying 'Verify your Redwood account' and I followed the link. The page asked for my API key and org id. I pasted my key into the form then got cold feet and closed the page. Rotated the key immediately in the Console but wanted to report here. @security-team :grimacing:

Priya S: Thanks for flagging, Maria. Can you paste the raw email headers (no need to redact) and the destination URL? Also which API key did you rotate (personal or service)?

Maria L: Pasted below. It was my personal user key (not a service key). URL: https://verify-redwood[dot]io/form/submit?id=redw-verify-3

--EMAIL HEADERS--
From: support@redwood-support.com
To: maria.l@redwood.com
Subject: Verify your Redwood account
Received-SPF: fail
Return-Path: bounce@verify-redwood.com

Maria L: The form POSTed to https://api[dot]collector-example.com/ingest. I did not hit submit after pasting; I think the form auto-recorded keystrokes? Not sure.

security-bot: Sandbox ticket created: SBX-2026-318. URL submitted for detonation. Priority: high.

Alex M: @security-bot can you also pull WHOIS & SSL cert info for verify-redwood[dot]io and collector domain?

security-bot: WHOIS: registrar: FastReg Ltd (privacy). SSL: cert issued 8 days ago, SANs include *.verify-redwood.io and collector-example.com. IPs: 18.205.33.12, 3.231.45.7.

Jonathan K: From initial look: domain is new and SPF fails. Collector domain hosted in cloud infra. More importantly — Maria, you said you rotated your key. Did you also search for any token uses in the last 30 minutes?

Maria L: I checked the Console usage page. No suspicious calls on that key after the time of exposure. Rotated at 14:03 UTC, last use logged at 13:58 UTC.

Dave R: Running quick audit: search for the exposed key across repos and recent pastebins. Using git grep and cloud logs.

Dave R: Ran grep and no hits. Searching audit logs for any API calls from your user id between 13:50-14:10 UTC...

--LOG QUERY (example)--
curl -H 'Authorization: Bearer $AUDIT_TOKEN' "https://console.redwood.com/api/v1/admin/audit?user=maria.l&since=2026-03-10T13:45:00Z&until=2026-03-10T14:15:00Z"

Dave R: No anomalous API activity. No KMS decrypt events tied to your principal in that window.

Priya S: Sandbox results in SBX-2026-318: the landing page includes JS that listens for input events and POSTs to collector-example.com/ingest with form data and some navigator metadata. No malware payload observed. The collector logs show received a POST with a non-Redwood API key string at 13:59:12 UTC. IP: 3.231.45.7.

Priya S: Verdict: credential harvester (client-side exfil) — low technical persistence but high data exposure risk. Action items below.

Alex M: Recommended containment checklist:
- Confirm rotated key has been revoked and replaced (Maria done).
- Revoke any active sessions/tokens for Maria (session IDs) and enforce re-login.
- Search audit logs for any activity from the collector IPs or that API key across the org (Dave assigned).
- Block domains at DNS/proxy (network team).
- Add collector domains to org-wide blocklist.
- Notify infra teams to check for KMS usage anomalies (even though Dave saw none).

Priya S: I'll draft an incident advisory for internal comms and include guidance: never paste API keys into forms, rotate keys, enable totp for Console, and enable short-lived credentials where possible.

Jonathan K: Also suggest we check for possible leakage into CI (maybe copied into a pipeline variable) and scan recent CI logs for the key string. If anyone else reported similar emails, escalate.

Dave R: I've run a quick CI artifact scan; no matches. Also added an alert rule to flag future requests matching the pattern of that collector endpoint.

Maria L: Thanks all. Appreciate the quick response. I already rotated and updated any saved keys in my keychain.

Priya S: I'll send the advisory to #general-security and include a short how-to for rotating keys and checking sessions. Also scheduling a 20-min drop-in demo tomorrow for the eng org on key hygiene.

Alex M: Follow-ups: (1) Network team to block domains (ticket NET-842). (2) SecOps to file a short post-incident note in Confluence with IOCs (domain, IPs, sample POST payload). (3) DevEx to add a Console modal warning when copying keys.

security-bot: SBX-2026-318 closed — behavior confirmed credential harvesting. IOCs: verify-redwood.io, collector-example.com, IPs: 3.231.45.7, 18.205.33.12.

Priya S: Closing the thread. Action items assigned: Dave -> continue sweeps for similar keys; Alex -> follow-up with network; Priya -> internal advisory and demo; Maria -> monitor account and report any oddities. Thanks :thumbsup:

Maria L: Thanks everyone :relieved:
